question.problem: Which root(s) of the polynomial $p(x)=16{x}^{3}-4{x}^{2}$ have multiplicity $1?$
question.worked_solution:
First, we need to factor the polynomial. 

For this polynomial, we can factor by noting that the greatest common factor of $16{x}^{3}$ and $-4{x}^{2}$ is $4{x}^{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}p(x) & =16{x}^{3}-4{x}^{2} \\  & =4{x}^{2}(4x-1)\end{aligned}
$$

To find the roots and their multiplicities, we look at the factors:

- The factor ${x}^{2}$ has an exponent of $2$ in the factored form of $p(x).$ So the root $x=0$ has multiplicity $2.$

- The factor $(4x-1)$ has an exponent of $1$ in the factored form of $p(x).$ So the root $x=\frac{1}{4}$ has multiplicity $1.$

In conclusion, only the root $x=\frac{1}{4}$ has multiplicity $1.$
